title: Congruent dissections of a triangle: prime counts, the counts up to 200, and a family of isosceles targets
description: A positive integer N is a tile count if some triangle can be cut into N pairwise congruent triangles; Erdős asked for the set of tile counts (Problem 634). The problem is not solved here. With every cited step checked in Lean 4 against the standard axioms only: (1) a prime p is a tile count if and only if p = 3 or p ≢ 3 (mod 4); (2) for 1 ≤ N ≤ 200 the tile counts are exactly 105 explicit values (the last value settled, 135, is excluded by a kernel-checked search certificate); (3) for a tile with angles (α, β, 2π/3), α/π irrational, a signed-direction functional gives two integrality conditions, and no prime number of such tiles tiles an isosceles, non-equilateral triangle; (4) for the base-β targets T_M(e,f) tiled by (ef, f²−e², f²), a tiling exists for every M ≥ f, none for M = 1, none when 2Me < f. Version 3.0 (papers `erdos634_v3W2` and `erdos634_v3C`) adds, with the label of each item given in the paper: tilings (in Lean) of W_M(e,f) and T_M(e,f) below the scale f for 2 ≤ e ≤ f−2 when Me ≥ f and (M−1)(f−e) ≥ f (sharp for e < f/2), a collar family for the base-α targets (the up-set in the scale is Paliy's), 27 further tile counts by macro pieces, the existence half of a conjectured classification of the tile counts (the exclusion half is open), no-tiling theorems for the thick regime (W_M(e,f), M < f, Me ≥ f, M(f−e) ≤ e+1: Lean, hand proof audited only inside the project; M(f−e) = e+2: hand proof only), exact-verified tilings showing 465·g² for g = 2, 3, 4 (so 465·g² for every g ≥ 2; Lean only for g ≥ 5), a census update (199,364 excluded / 129,108 tile counts / 63,602 undecided among the non-squarefree N ≤ 10^6 by Lean-formal exclusions; 199,441 / 129,108 / 63,525 with the hand-proved class), exact computer evidence on one open family, and a list of corrections. Version 3.1 adds, with labels in RELEASE_NOTES_v3.1.md: a Lean aggregate (windowed exclusions of 67 values up to 10^5, unaudited; 465·g² and 7672·g² for every g ≥ 2), the census 199,364 / 129,117 / 63,593 (67 exclusions Lean-formal), and a note on a computer-assisted case tree for one rung of the thick regime (not a theorem). Version 4.0 adds a band theorem for the base-β targets T_M(e,f) (Lean, internal audit only; the Lean files are in the public repository ElVec1o/formalizing-triangle-tiling-in-lean), a curated registry extract of 3,204 excluded instances, and a census update (200,282 excluded / 62,421 undecided among the non-squarefree N ≤ 10^6); the paper `erdos634_v3C` is version 4.0. Version 5.0 (1 November 2026) adds, with labels in RELEASE_NOTES_v5.0.md and docs/CLAIMS_5.0.md: an up-set theorem for the isosceles targets with base angle α and apex angle 2α at every coprime pair u < v < 2u (cap, slice and strip construction; hand proof, AI-assisted internal audit, not formalized in Lean; it needs Theorem D' and reflections of the tile), a collar at (2,3) (T(g) is tiled by 5g² copies of (4,5,6) for every g ≥ 12) and a thin-W base lemma (Lean, internal audit only, standard axioms, no outside check), 117 further explicit tile counts with exact-verified witnesses or regenerating recipes (40 of them, Zhang's, also as Lean instances that are kernel-checked with the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound but NOT audited), a census update (200,282 excluded / 129,420 known / 62,372 undecided among the non-squarefree N ≤ 10^6), and a supplement paper erdos634_v5_supplement; nothing is claimed about the prime case beyond version 4.0, nor about the full problem. The prime case is unchanged: no prime p ≡ 3 (mod 4), p > 3, is a tile count. A proof of (1) was first made public by D. Paliy on 29 September 2026; the proof here was obtained independently; M. Beeson and G. Roșu (arXiv:2607.23453, v2 16 and v3 21 October 2026) state a result on the prime tile counts, about whose proof nothing is claimed here. The repository contains the paper, the Lean library, the certificate manifest with a regeneration script, and the Rust search and replay programs. The work was carried out with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic) throughout, under the author's direction.
